html:
A famine in the breakaway state of Biafra in southeastern Nigeria during the Nigerian Civil War of 1967 to 1970. Estimates of the civilians who died of hunger and disease run from half a million to two million; a million is often given.

Biafra declared independence in 1967 under Odumegwu Ojukwu, after massacres of Igbo people in the north. The federal government blockaded it by land, sea and air, and as federal troops closed in, Biafra shrank and filled with refugees. Food ran out, and children wasted from kwashiorkor, a disease of protein starvation.

Photographs of starving children were among the first famine images seen on television around the world. Churches flew food in at night to a jungle airstrip in the Biafran airlift. Some French doctors who worked in Biafra and felt bound to speak out went on to found Médecins Sans Frontières in 1971. Biafra surrendered in January 1970.
sum: A famine in the breakaway state of Biafra in southeastern Nigeria during the Nigerian Civil War of 1967 to 1970. Estimates of the civilians who died of hunger and disease run from half a million to two million; a million is often given.
